The world

Meta Brand Building Summit / B&T, eMarketer · October 16, 2026

Meta rebuilds the single-sponsor TV time slot inside the feed

Meta announced Ads Super Burst, letting advertisers book a concentrated window of three to 24 hours through its Reach Planner with guaranteed delivery and, critically, category exclusivity: no competing advertiser can book the same window. In testing, campaigns reached a median of 34 million people with a 2.9 percentage-point lift in ad recall. Alongside it, Meta rolled out First Impression Ads (one advertiser a day gets the first ad slot when someone opens Facebook Feed, US test) and expanded Reels Trending Ads to 15 content categories, including Home & Garden and Spanish-language content for the first time.

Why it mattersCategory exclusivity for a fixed window is not a new idea, it’s the oldest idea in broadcast, a single sponsor owning a slot so no rival can be seen anywhere near it. Meta just rebuilt that inside a feed that never had fixed time slots to begin with.
ppc.land · October 8-10, 2026

IAB Tech Lab calls its Apple workaround “production ready” with nothing shipped

After Apple’s iOS 27 quietly blocked The Trade Desk’s ad domain and roughly a dozen other ad-tech and identity companies in Safari (covered in issue 16), IAB Tech Lab CEO Anthony Katsur posted on X on October 8 that the Lab’s server-side workaround, Trusted Server, “is production ready TODAY!” Its public GitHub repository shows 343 commits, 130 branches and zero published releases. Separately, Apple’s own fix for The Trade Desk specifically, tested October 5 in an iOS 27.2 beta, still needs that beta to become the live install base before it means anything, which industry trackers estimate is three to four weeks out.

Why it mattersAn industry body telling publishers to move their entire ad stack onto “production ready” software that has never had a formal release is the same kind of unverifiable precision claim this issue keeps running into, confidence standing in for proof.
beinsure.com / PYMNTS · October 5, 2026

Google and the DOJ still can’t agree on how fast the ad tech remedies happen

Judge Leonie Brinkema’s September ruling ordered Google to open its ad exchange to rivals, but the two sides filed competing versions of the final implementation order on October 5. The DOJ wants the AdX-Prebid connection live within 6 months and global rollout from day one; Google wants 12 months domestically and 24 more months before going global. They also disagree on when publishers get Google’s ad-server data (while evaluating a switch, per the DOJ, or only after deciding to switch, per Google) and on how fast Google must respond to a compliance monitor’s requests (14 days per the DOJ, 30 per Google). Brinkema has to resolve the gap before signing anything; Google is expected to appeal regardless.

Why it matters“Google must open its ad exchange” sounded like the end of the story last month. The actual fight, over whether that happens in 6 months or 36, is the part that decides whether the remedy changes anything real.
TechRadar / eMarketer · October 17, 2026

Instagram wires song discovery straight into Spotify

Instagram’s integration with Spotify rolled out globally today for iOS and Android: tap a song name on a post or Reel, and a single button adds it to the listener’s Spotify Liked Songs, no Premium subscription required. Stories gets audio previews of shared tracks, and Instagram Notes now shows what a friend is currently listening to in real time.

Why it mattersInstagram isn’t trying to keep that attention for itself anymore, it’s routing it somewhere else with one tap. For a platform that spent years trying to out-music TikTok with its own sound library, handing the discovery moment straight to Spotify is a quiet admission of what it isn’t going to win.

Campaigns & brand moves

spotandweb.it Telex Pubblicità · October 16, 2026, Italy

Nutella brings a year-old TV spot back for bakery season

Ferrero’s “Pane e Nutella” project, built with the University of Gastronomic Sciences of Pollenzo, adds ten new regional bread video-stories (completing twenty in total) with Fabio Volo fronting the social push. From October 16 the 60-second TV spot that first aired in 2025 returns, alongside two new 20-second cuts, running through November 1 across 832 screens in 14 train stations spanning 11 regions, plus packaging and 1,300 partner bakeries.

Why it mattersReviving last year’s spot instead of shooting a new one isn’t a budget shortcut here, it’s the point. The whole project is about bread as inherited craft, so the ad gets to inherit itself too.
Contagious case study · October 12, 2026, Germany

Penny turns its funniest TikTok comments into real money

Penny and agencies Saint Elmo’s and Charles & Charlotte ran “Comment Coupons” against the brand platform “Echte Freude” (Real Joy): an AI system scored TikTok comments on humor, likes, replies and relevance to the original post, then rewarded the best ones with shopping vouchers worth up to €50. The brand identified more than 4,000 standout comments and paid out €45,000 in total.

Why it mattersMost brands treat the comment section as something to moderate. Penny treated it as inventory worth paying for, which is a different definition of what the ad actually is.

Bayer Italia turns dead time into cardiac-health awareness

YAM112003 · from October 15, 2026, Italy

“Trova il tempo per conoscere l’amiloidosi cardiaca” (Find the time to learn about cardiac amyloidosis) runs as DOOH in Milan, Rome and Naples, placed specifically in subways, airports, stations and other transit points where people are already waiting with nothing to do.

Why it mattersThe media plan is the creative idea here. A disease most people have never heard of gets explained in exactly the stretch of time someone would otherwise spend staring at a wall.

What is working in content

Contagious Brands Report 2026 · published October 4, 2026

Brands are turning stores into the content, not the backdrop for it

Contagious’s annual report selected 45 brands across nine categories; “Destination Designers” groups brands that rebuilt physical retail as a place worth visiting on its own terms. Gentle Monster now runs 84 stores worldwide, each one a standalone art installation with hidden product, selling through 450+ retailers in 30 countries on the strength of that reputation. Dick’s Sporting Goods rebuilt locations as sports playgrounds; Miniso Land opened 26 stores built around a theme-park concept.

Why it mattersNone of these stores are optimized to move product fastest, they’re optimized to be filmed and shared. The store became the content format, which means the metric that matters shifted from footfall-to-purchase to footfall-to-post.

Meta’s own data shows which content categories are worth chasing right now

Meta Brand Building Summit · October 16, 2026, self-reported

Inside the same announcement as Ads Super Burst (above), Meta expanded Reels Trending Ads, which let brands piggyback on trending audio, to 15 content categories, newly including Home & Garden and Spanish-language content. Meta’s own testing shows those campaigns delivering five-plus percentage-point lifts in both action intent and unaided brand awareness.

Why it mattersIt’s Meta’s own number, not an independent study, flagged as such, but it’s also a direct signal of where the platform wants attention to go next. Home & Garden and Spanish-language are the categories Meta is actively building tools to feed.

Social trends

Be OK (TikTok)

  • Clips set to Ingrid Michaelson’s upbeat track “Be OK,” paired with everyday moments reframed as small personal wins, from finishing a hard week to surviving a bad date.
Why it mattersThe whole trend is a mood edit, not a story. The song supplies the arc so the creator doesn’t have to build one.

Pray For Me Slow Mo (TikTok)

  • Group-participation format: a slow-motion clip of someone about to do something minor and mildly risky (a jump, a prank, a confession), captioned “pray for me,” while the people around them react in real time.
Why it mattersSlow motion turns a two-second moment into a shared countdown, buying the format just enough suspense to justify the group reaction shot.

Shaving Cream Prank Reveal (TikTok)

  • A couples/family prank built on a fake-out: one person feigns a small, mild gesture, then gets hit with a full handful of shaving cream when they let their guard down.
Why it mattersThe setup is the joke. Everyone online already knows the prank genre well enough that the format can spend its first few seconds pretending to be something gentler, and the audience waits for the turn.

The historical bridge

New York, 1948

The single sponsor who owned the whole time slot

On June 8, 1948, Texaco took its radio variety show Texaco Star Theater to television on NBC, built on an advertising model J. Walter Thompson had already proven on radio: one sponsor, one show, total ownership. No competitor could buy time anywhere near it; Texaco’s uniformed service attendants opened every episode, folded straight into the entertainment instead of interrupting it. Milton Berle became the host, and by 1949 the show was pulling as much as 80% of the entire US television viewing audience on the nights it aired. Texaco kept the sponsorship exclusive until 1953, when Buick took over and the show was renamed around its new, equally singular owner.

Why it still holds. Meta’s Ads Super Burst (above) sells advertisers the same thing JWT sold Texaco in 1948: a fixed window where no competitor can appear, at a scale usually reserved for television. The only thing that changed in 78 years is that the “time slot” used to mean a Tuesday night and now means three to 24 hours inside an algorithmic feed, the exclusivity is the product either way.
